metricDefinitions.FALSE_IDENTITY_RATE: an exact-identity route returned a pinned result for an identifier CONFIRMED ABSENT from the corpus. Threshold zero. This is the failure that matters: a ranked list says "these are the closest things I hold"; an exact route says "this is the case you named".
metricDefinitions.NON_EMPTY_RATE: the ranked arm returned something. Reported as BEHAVIOUR, never as pass/fail — /search returns authorities, not answers, and a page of near-misses is often the correct product response to a query about law nobody has held.

results.query: My client is a 29 year old man working in a private firm in Bengaluru. He met the complainant through a colleague in 2021 and they were in a relationship for about three years, during which they travelled together on several occasions, and both families were aware. In 2024 the relationship broke down after his parents refused the match on caste grounds. In 2025 the complainant lodged a first information report alleging that the entire relationship had been on a false promise of marriage and that consent had therefore been vitiated. The investigating officer filed a charge sheet without recording the complainant's parents, who had earlier told the police that they knew of the relationship. My client now seeks to have the proceedings quashed. I need the authorities on when a consensual relationship between adults that later breaks down can be treated as consent obtained under a misconception of fact, and in particular whether the complainant's own conduct, education and social background are relevant to that assessment.

The accused was arrested in March 2021 in a case involving an alleged trespass and assault at his company premises during a celebration. The investigation dragged on for nearly five years without a final report being filed, and no reasons for the delay were ever recorded or intimated to the Magistrate. In the meantime the accused has been required to attend the police station repeatedly and his business has suffered. He now wants a direction that the investigation be concluded within a fixed time, or in the alternative that the proceedings be brought to an end. I need the provisions that impose outer limits on the duration of an investigation under the new criminal procedure code, whether those limits are mandatory or directory, and what a High Court can do when an investigating officer has simply not complied with them.

My clients took premises on what they say was an oral lease running from 2018. They paid a sum described in correspondence as an advance towards the transfer of leasehold rights, and there is a WhatsApp exchange in which the other side calls it an advance. The premises were vacated in June 2022 and possession handed over, but the money was never refunded, and a cheque issued in September 2023 towards repayment was dishonoured. The commercial court decreed recovery. On appeal we say there was never a lease at all, because no instrument was executed and no stamp duty was paid, and that the amount was adjusted against transfer expenses. I need authorities on whether an oral lease can be proved where a local law requires an instrument, and on whether an admitted receipt of money can be retained by simply describing it as an advance.

PASTED FROM AN OPPONENT'S WRITTEN SUBMISSIONS: "It is well settled that where the cognizance of the case has in fact been taken and the case has proceeded to termination, the invalidity of the precedent investigation does not vitiate the result, unless miscarriage of justice has been caused thereby. The learned Special Public Prosecutor submits that if cognizance is in fact taken on a Police Report vitiated by the breach of a mandatory provision relating to investigation, there can be no doubt that the result of the trial which follows it cannot be set aside unless the illegality in the investigation can be shown to have brought about a miscarriage of justice." — which judgment is this passage taken from, and is it still good law?

PASTED FROM A DRAFT: "The BNSS has introduced a strict regime of time-bound investigation. Section 193(1) mandates that every investigation shall be completed without unnecessary delay; Section 193(2) that in relation to offences punishable with imprisonment of seven years or more the investigation shall ordinarily be completed within ninety days, and in all other offences within sixty days; and Section 193(3) that if the investigation is not completed within the prescribed period the investigating officer shall record the reasons in writing and intimate the Magistrate." — find me the judgment this is drawn from and any High Court that has taken a different view.

PASTED: "the accused must have mens rea to instigate the deceased to commit suicide. The act of instigation must be of such intensity that it is intended to push the deceased to such a position under which he or she has no choice but to commit suicide. Such instigation must be in proximity to the act of committing suicide." — is this the current formulation, and which authorities state it?
Which code applies to my client's case?
